benchmark.category: a virtual fitting room for a LARP and fantasy-gear marketplace
benchmark.users: LARP and cosplay shoppers building a kit who want to see gear on themselves, filter by fit, price and style, and change the look by chat or voice before buying

requirements.source_phrase: Variable `data` is potentially used before assignment at lines 285, 286, and 287 in the `assistant()` function
requirements.statement: POST /api/fitting-room/assistant returns a JSON body carrying a reply for every request shape — a body with no message, an empty history, empty equipped and benched lists, and an unexpected model response — and never a 500 from an uninitialised local or an empty response body.
requirements.notes: Critical review finding: an unbound local on some branches of assistant(). R-063 covers provider failure; this covers request-shape and branch coverage that never reaches the provider. Hard to test because the failing branch is only hit by particular message/history combinations, so probe several bodies including an empty one.

requirements.source_phrase: Using `is` instead of `==` to compare constant literals in `list_products()` function
requirements.statement: GET /api/fitting-room/products matches each supplied filter value against the stored value by equality — category=helmet returns exactly the helmet items, a category value absent from the catalog returns an empty list rather than the whole catalog, min_price=0 imposes no lower bound, and an omitted or empty-string parameter applies no restriction.
requirements.notes: R-010 pins combined-filter correctness; this pins the identity-vs-equality and zero/empty-parameter cases the review flags at lines 111, 114, 125, 126. Test with min_price=0 and category='' because those are the paths an `is` comparison breaks while an interned literal can appear to work.

requirements.source_phrase: Break down `assistant()` into smaller helper functions for each logic branch
requirements.statement: After the refactor, GET /api/fitting-room/products with any combination of filters, GET /api/fitting-room/facets, GET /api/fitting-room/products/{id}, POST /api/fitting-room/assistant and POST /api/fitting-room/tryon each answer with a JSON body and a status from their own contract — none returns a 500, an undefined-name error or an empty body.
requirements.notes: The review also asks that list_products arguments move into a configuration object/dataclass and that try_on validation be extracted; the observable outcome of all three refactors is that the same five routes keep answering the same requests. Contract details stay in R-010, R-013, R-006, R-002 and R-056; this requirement only forbids a route that stops answering.

requirements.statement: Reopening the measurements form in the same session and saving after changing only the gender/fit selector stores the newly selected gender, keeps the previously saved height and weight, updates the measurement tag and re-filters the catalog to that gender plus unisex on that same save.
requirements.notes: The stale-closure finding is observable exactly here: a gender captured in a stale closure saves the old value. Pairs with R-095 (gender sets the catalog filter) and R-099 (edit without a new selfie). Run it after a first save so the stale value would be the first gender.

requirements.statement: Each user message and each assistant reply appears at the bottom of the chat's visible area without the user scrolling, earlier messages stay above it, and this holds when several messages arrive in a row while a reply is still pending.
requirements.notes: Stale listRef/scrollTo is observable as a chat that stops scrolling new replies into view. R-036 requires history to remain visible; this requires the newest turn to be reachable without manual scrolling, checked with a chat long enough to overflow.

requirements.source_phrase: `src/features/fitting-room/StylistChat.jsx:53` - Using array index as React key
requirements.statement: After several turns each chat bubble shows its own text and its own role (user or Quartermaster) in send order, and a re-render or a queued reply never moves one message's text into another bubble and never drops a bubble.
requirements.notes: Index keys surface as text shifting between bubbles once the list grows or is reordered. Check after at least three turns and after two fast consecutive messages so a queued reply is appended.

requirements.source_phrase: `src/features/fitting-room/SelfieMirror.jsx:81` - Using array index as React key
requirements.statement: Removing one row from the selection strip or the equipped tray leaves every remaining row showing its own item's name, photo, price and size, and the removed item's row disappears with no other row taking on different content.
requirements.notes: Index keys are observable when the list shrinks: the row after the removed one can inherit the wrong photo and price. Uses the outfit-list testids from R-076 and a strip of at least three distinct-priced items.

requirements.statement: Capturing a selfie with the camera stops the camera stream when the camera view closes, closing and reopening the camera view twice leaves one active stream rather than two, and the most recent capture becomes the model source used by the next preview.
requirements.notes: Missing media-stream dependencies are observable as a camera light that stays on and a duplicated stream on reopen. Headless runs exercise the file-upload path; the camera path is confirmed by code review plus checking that only one stream is created across a close/reopen cycle.

requirements.source_phrase: Creates new array references on every render, causing unnecessary re-renders
requirements.statement: The catalog filter option lists for category, gender, color and aesthetic show the same values in the same order on every render, and choosing one filter value leaves the other filters' selected values and their option lists unchanged rather than resetting or reordering them.
requirements.notes: Inline array props are observable as a select whose options reorder or whose selection is lost when another control changes. The option values themselves come from R-056 and must still equal the catalog facets.

requirements.statement: While a try-on is generating, the loading indicator advances through successive stage messages instead of freezing on the first, and it disappears when the preview image arrives or the request fails.
requirements.notes: R-046 requires a progress state; this pins the stale-closure failure where the stage never changes. Acceptance: at least two distinct stage texts observed during one generation, then no indicator once the image renders. Budget the test to the try-on calls the change allows (one happy path).

requirements.statement: Serving the production build produces no console.warn or console.log statements of the app's own, so a user's browser console stays free of the review's build-time warnings while the fitting room and catalog work.
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class item the review requests; check by loading the built app and reading the browser console, and by scanning the served configuration. The agent context note keeps the `is not None` comparisons and the shadcn use-toast.js console usage out of scope, so only the app's own build warnings count.

requirements.statement: One outfit change — equip, take off, swap or remove — produces exactly one preview regeneration, and when changes are made in quick succession the preview ends showing the final worn set rather than an earlier intermediate one.
requirements.notes: Build description and the review of index.jsx useMemo (lines 19, 49), useEffect (lines 51, 56, 169) and useCallback (line 64) dependencies: the fixes can regress into duplicate or out-of-order generations that also double provider cost. Derived from the build, not from a user line. Keep to two try-on calls: one single change, then one rapid sequence, and check the last image matches the final worn set.
